Key Learning: High: CG has rich heritage of indigenous rice. Crucial for tribal seed sovereignty.
Remark: Seed sovereignty reduces dependency on market and preserves genetic resilience.

Name: Innovative Farmer (Story 37)
Climatic Conditions: Drought Prone/Dry
Innovation And Practice Uses: organic farming through dry land cultivation: mulching, fym, sowing before monsoon.
Result: Retaining soil moisture in water-scarce regions.
Applicability in Chhattisgarh: Productivity rose by 2 quintals/ha; Profit up Rs 5,000/acre; 20% less labor.
Key Learning: High: Relevant for rainfed districts like Rajnandgaon and Kawardha.
Remark: Mulching and organic carbon are critical for drought resilience.

Name: Bhaskar Save / Ashok Sanghavi
Climatic Conditions: Wasteland/Coastal
Innovation And Practice Uses: rehabilitation of wasteland: "natural farming" - no till, organic mulch, intercrops.
Result: Converting barren land into productive orchard.
Applicability in Chhattisgarh: Production in 3 years vs 7 years; Soil generated from wasteland.
Key Learning: High: Applicable for reclaiming degraded lands or mining-affected areas in CG.
Remark: Nature-compatible farming (Permaculture) restores soil health fastest.

Name: Sabarkantha
Climatic Conditions: Wadi (Orchard)with Vermicomposting & Farm Bunding
Innovation And Practice Uses: diversified income source beyond traditional farming.
Result: Income funded daughter's nursing education; bought 6 livestock.
Applicability in Chhattisgarh: Very High: Direct match for "Wadi" programs in CG tribal districts.
Key Learning: Fruit trees act as a financial safety net for long-term family goals.

Name: Ms. Jyoti Dang
Climatic Conditions: Rainfed / Hilly Tribal Belt
Innovation And Practice Uses: permaculture & resource integration: combined organic millet farming with a backyard vermicompost unit and local poultry to ensure a self-sustaining cycle of soil fertility.
Result: Secured a consistent livelihood and food security for her family; demonstrated that landless women can prosper through smart leasing of fallow land.
Applicability in Chhattisgarh: High. Perfect for landless tribal women in Chhattisgarh who can work as Self-Help Groups (SHGs) to lease and restore fallow village lands.
Key Learning: Land ownership is not a prerequisite for success; millets are the ultimate poverty-alleviation crop for the landless.
Remark: A powerful example of a single mother achieving independence through resilient and low-cost agricultural practices.

Name: Mr. Guddu Dongare
Location: Village Pipala, District Betul, Madhya Pradesh
Climatic Conditions: Semi-Arid and Drought-Prone
Innovation And Practice Uses: fallow land utilization: converted unproductive hilly land into a profit center by adopting row farming and utilizing local organic manures instead of chemical fertilizers.
Result: Achieved a yield of 12 quintals per hectare and an overall profit of 10,000 rupees from land that was previously lying idle.
Applicability in Chhattisgarh: High. Chhattisgarh has vast tracts of hilly fallow lands (Tikra/Bari) that can be converted into millet hubs with zero input cost.
Key Learning: Unproductive and fallow lands are hidden assets; millets are the perfect crop to restore soil health without expensive irrigation.
Remark: This model was supported by Farmer Field Schools which provided technical training to the local community.

Name: Mr. Badal Sahoo
Climatic Conditions: Rainfed and Semi-Arid
Innovation And Practice Uses: system of millets intensification (smi): used home-made bio-inputs such as jeevamrutha and bijamrutha to eliminate chemical dependence and focused on community-led seed preservation.
Result: Successfully mobilized 25 farmers to adopt sustainable practices; achieved a 10 quintal yield per acre with minimal financial investment.
Applicability in Chhattisgarh: Very High. Chhattisgarh’s "Millet Mission" relies on this specific CRP (Community Resource Person) model for tribal outreach and Gauthans for bio-inputs.
Key Learning: Local youth can drive massive agricultural shifts by demonstrating low-cost organic success on their own small plots.
Remark: Shows that returning to traditional organic roots is more profitable than chemical-intensive industrial farming.
